claims.text: Applying a functionally graded ceramic coating by plasma spraying improves the surface hardness of metallic components in aggressive service environments.
Applying a functionally graded ceramic coating by plasma spraying improves the wear resistance of metallic components in aggressive service environments.
The proposed coating has a graded microstructure with a dense, crack-resistant top layer.
The coating gradually transitions to the metallic substrate.
The graded transition reduces residual stresses in the coating system.
The ceramic coating acts as a physical barrier that impedes ingress of corrosive species.
The ceramic coating mechanically reinforces the component surface.
Barrier protection and mechanical reinforcement reduce crack initiation under thermal and mechanical loads.
Barrier protection and mechanical reinforcement reduce crack propagation under thermal and mechanical loads.
The coating is expected to produce approximately 30–50% greater surface hardness than an untreated, polished surface.
The coating is expected to produce approximately 30–50% greater wear resistance than an untreated, polished surface.
The expected improvements apply under combined high-temperature, high-humidity, and corrosive-chemical exposure.
The improvement may diminish under extreme cyclic thermal loading.
The improvement may diminish under sustained high-impact stress that exceeds the coating's toughness limits.
The magnitude of improvement depends on coating thickness, plasma-spray parameters, and environmental conditions.
